summary: Made the loaded model's lifetime equal the print flow's: added AppViewModel.leavePrintSetup() as the single exit from Print setup (used by its arrow and by system back), which asks before throwing the model away, and clearModel(discardFiles = true) now deletes the imported cache copy plus last_model_path/last_gcode_path (Files-owned and demo files stay). Home's model row became LoadedModelRow: open the flow it belongs to, Replace, or Discard (Replace kept per review; Discard hidden while a print needs the model or in demo mode). Also added PrintJobState.isInProgress as the one answer to 'is something printing?' - the first device build used live && !isTerminal and treated an idle-but-answerable printer as a running print, which silently skipped the new dialog; Home's banner and the print-setup exit now share the new property.

Gave the Files tab a G-code shelf: GcodeHistoryStore files every finished slice into filesDir/gcodes with a JSON manifest (newest first, 10 files / 200 MB), AppViewModel.persistSliceResult now adopts the archived path instead of leaving the g-code in cacheDir behind last_gcode_path, and discarding a model no longer deletes a filed slice. LibraryScreen's model row became a shared FileRow/FileTile pair so Models and G-code render identically, plus SlicedGcode with its delete confirmation. Built and installed on the Pixel 4a: the shelf listed three slices and opening one rendered its preview (screenshots reviewed in chat; the first shot showed the row detail truncating the date, so the printer name came off that line). The cache-to-archive move in record() is only code-reviewed - verifying it needs a real slice, recorded as the node's next step.

Gave every g-code row its own picture. preview/GcodePreviewImage.kt renders a g-code to a 192px PNG - the PNG a slicer embedded in the file when it has one (decoded by the new GcodeThumbnail.readPng, which now understands the standard "; thumbnail begin WxH len" block Prusa and Bambu write, not only the app's own marker), otherwise the parsed toolpaths drawn flat like the 3D preview does. GcodeHistoryStore stores that as thumbs/<name>.png next to the g-code, keeps the absolute path on the entry (setThumb, thumbPath on the record path too), and gains renderMissingThumbs() with an unrenderable set so a file that yields nothing is not reparsed on every start; AppViewModel.renderGcodeThumbs() runs it on Dispatchers.IO at init, so slices filed before previews existed get theirs on the next launch and a new slice's tile fills in without stalling the UI. LibraryScreen's FileTile now takes a path instead of a pre-decoded bitmap and decodes it at inSampleSize 4, which both shelves share, so G-code rows show the print instead of a printer glyph. Fixed the compile errors the previous batch left (BitmapFactory bounds decode used as if it returned Options, a scope refactor that dropped layers/stride, an unresolved setThumb); :app:assembleDebug is green, installed on the Pixel 4a and the shelf now renders previews for all three seeded slices (screenshot reviewed in chat).

Fixed the back route the G-code shelf left wrong. Opening an archived slice put the app on Screen.Preview, whose parent was hardcoded to Slice and then print setup - a page with no model in it, because opening a filed g-code never takes the model through that flow. AppViewModel now carries previewReturnTo, set by showPreview() (Home by default, Slice from the slice flow, Library from the shelf) and used by goBack(); the preview's own button routes through the same field and names the place - "Back to Files" - instead of always saying "Back to home", with a Screen.backLabel extension supplying the wording. Verified on the Pixel 4a: Files -> G-code -> row opens the preview, and both the system bar and the button return to the G-code shelf (screenshots in chat); the slice-flow route keeps its old target and still needs a real slice to re-check.

Print setup: the Printer and Process pickers moved to the bottom of the settings card and now show their whole values. Both were singleLine ExposedDropdownMenu fields, so the machine read "Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 0" and the preset "0.24mm Draft @Elegoo CC2..." - the one place that names which slicer preset a slice will use was unreadable. Design.kt's DropdownRow now allows two wrapped lines (AdvancedSettings and every other dropdown inherits it), and PrintSetupScreen orders the card Material, Build plate, Quality, Printer, Process so the machine and preset sit next to the button that uses them. Verified on the Pixel 4a with multi_clip.3mf loaded: header shows the full "Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 0.4 nozzle" and "0.20mm Standard @Elegoo CC2 0.4 nozzle" above Next: Slice (screenshot in chat).

Implemented UI/UX quick-win fixes: rebuilt PrintSetupFullscreen with inset-safe top readout, bottom tool dock (Face/Rotate/Mirror/Move), and legible Reset; switched AdvancedSettings multi-option fields (Infill pattern, Adhesion, Seam position) from SegmentedControl to DropdownRow and removed blank leadingIcon indent in Design.DropdownRow; fixed SliceScreen top-bar Back to call vm.goBack() (returns to Print setup); fixed SwitchRow double-click wiring using Modifier.toggleable + null Switch callback and restored ripple indication across Design.kt controls; made LibraryScreen G-code count reactive via collectAsState(); made DeviceStatusScreen body scrollable with pinned top bar and bottom action.
verdict: testDebugUnitTest + assembleDebug green; PrintSetupFullscreen, AdvancedSettings dropdowns, Files tab, and SliceScreen back arrow verified on Pixel 4a (screenshots reviewed); DeviceStatusScreen scroll is compile/code-reviewed only

summary: Fixed two device bugs: (1) Case light reliability while printing: serialized CloudPrintManager.ensureLoggedIn with a Mutex so concurrent camera heartbeats don't race light commands, added 12s optimistic lightOn hold + partial-frame lightOn preservation in AppViewModel so stale 5s cloud polls/MQTT don't snap the toggle back, added automatic retry + visible error/revert on Cloud light failure, added retry-until-confirmed on LAN method 1029, and parsed flat/nested led status/power/brightness shapes in LanPrintMonitor.mergePrintStatus; (2) Window insets / content sliding behind status & nav bars: switched to enableEdgeToEdge() once in MainActivity.onCreate() instead of per-recomposition setDecorFitsSystemWindows in Theme.kt, added screenLayout|smallestScreenSize to configChanges + requestApplyInsets in onConfigurationChanged and CameraFullscreen.onDispose, removed 140ms fade delay on CameraFullscreen transitions, added safeDrawingPadding on CameraFullscreen controls, added navigationBarsPadding on PrintSetupScreen bottomBar, and added status/nav bar padding on AllCommentsDialog.
verdict: testDebugUnitTest + assembleDebug green; pushed and installed on Pixel 4a for verification

summary: Fixed printer connection stability, case light firmware compatibility, and Cloud RTC camera handling: MqttManager single-client lifecycle + reconnect re-subscribe + led/temp/fan delta parsing + seedPrintStatus; AppViewModel deduped startMqtt/checkSession, reused live cloud monitors without Connecting flicker, kept active prints monitored on background, dual power+brightness method 1029 payload, cameraVideoReady state; LanPrintMonitor auto-reconnect + dual light payload; CloudPrintManager credential cache + RTM auto-reconnect; CloudAuthClient mutex refreshTokens; CloudRtcCamera TextureView + ChannelMediaOptions (AUDIENCE) + main-thread setupRemoteVideo + waiting indicator in CameraStage; PrinterScreen reactive filaments; unit tests in LanPrintMonitorTest.
verdict: testDebugUnitTest + assembleDebug green; verified live on Pixel 4a (single MQTT client, stable connection, case light working; confirmed cloud video stream currently offline in official Matrix app too)
